content.text: No sourcing-exclusivity obligation on Customer exists anywhere; §12.3 affirmatively negates one. Submitting compliant at the preferred level.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no exclusivity, sole-supplier, requirements, or "shall not procure from any third party" obligation binding Customer. §12.3 (p0044) goes further and expressly preserves our freedom to acquire, license or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, with Vendor acknowledging that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment; the only "exclusive" references elsewhere are the non-exclusive licence grant to us (§13.1), non-exclusive remedies, and forum clauses, none of which bind our sourcing. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. Two adjacent terms were checked and deliberately not flagged here: §7.2 (p0026) is a disclose-and-match mechanic on more favourable competing offers, which is an MFN/right-to-match term rather than a prohibition on using alternative providers, and belongs under the MFN rule; §12.4 (p0046) is a non-compete/field-of-use covenant on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products, which is the restrictive-covenant term addressed under the non-compete rule and should not be double-flagged as sourcing exclusivity (it is also expressly contradicted by §12.3).

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
